# Strategic Initiative Tracking Process

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../README.md) • [Governance](../README.md) • [Processes](./README.md)**

---

> The Strategic Initiative Tracking Process provides a centralized mechanism for monitoring and managing enterprise architecture initiatives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, tracking progress, and maintaining visibility across all stakeholders.

---
page_texts.2:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#process-overview]

## Process Overview

**Purpose**: To establish a systematic approach for tracking architecturally significant strategic EA initiatives from inception through completion, ensuring transparency, accountability, and alignment with enterprise architecture strategy and organizational objectives.

**Scope**: This process tracks only initiatives deemed **architecturally significant** by the assigned Solution Architect. Architectural significance is defined by the Qualifying Activities criteria in the [Concept Review Board](../governing-bodies/concept-review-board.md#qualifying-activities) and [Architecture Review Board](../governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#qualifying-activities) Applicability sections; Solution Architects apply professional judgment to determine which initiatives beyond those mandatory triggers also warrant EA oversight and monitoring.

**Charter**: This process is chartered to:

- Maintain a centralized repository of architecturally significant strategic EA initiatives
- Track initiative status, progress, and dependencies
- Monitor resource allocation and capacity planning
- Identify risks, blockers, and mitigation strategies
- Facilitate communication and stakeholder engagement
- Support prioritization and decision-making
- Enable reporting and metrics collection
- Ensure alignment with strategic goals and roadmaps

**Process Type**: Strategic Governance

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#process-flow]

## Process Flow

| Step   | Activity                                | Owner                      | Duration    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------- |
| **1**  | Identify strategic initiative           | Business Area Lead         | 1-2 days    |
| **2**  | Assess architectural significance       | Solution Architect (SA)    | 1-2 days    |
| **3**  | Create initiative entry in tracker      | Solution Architect (SA)    | 1 day       |
| **4**  | Define scope, objectives, and metrics   | Solution Architect (SA)    | 3-5 days    |
| **5**  | Review and approve initiative           | EA Governance Lead         | 1 week      |
| **6**  | Regular status updates                  | Solution Architect (SA)    | Weekly      |
| **7**  | Monthly progress review                 | EA Governance Lead         | Monthly     |
| **8**  | Identify and manage dependencies        | Solution Architect (SA)    | Continuous  |
| **9**  | Track risks and implement mitigations   | Solution Architect (SA)    | Continuous  |
| **10** | Update completion status                | Solution Architect (SA)    | As achieved |

**Total Process Time**: Variable (project-dependent)
**Trigger Events**: New strategic initiative approved, major program launch, architectural transformation, compliance requirement

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#required-information]

### Required Information

Each initiative tracked in the system must include:
page_texts.11:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#basic-information]

#### Basic Information

| Field Name | Data Type | Required | Description | Notes |
| ---------- | --------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- |
| **Business Area** | Choice/Lookup | Yes | Business capability area | Separate SharePoint list maintained for each area |
| **Initiative ID** | Auto-Number | Auto | Unique identifier | Automatically assigned by system |
| **Title** | Single Line Text | Yes | Clear, descriptive initiative name | - |
| **Description** | Multiple Lines Text | Yes | High-level explanation of the initiative, its purpose, and expected outcomes | - |
| **Effort Size** | Choice | Yes | Estimated duration | Small (1-3 months), Medium (4-8 months), Large (9+ months) |
| **Owner** | Person/Lookup | Yes | Business owner accountable for the initiative | - |
| **Solution Architect** | Person/Lookup | Yes | SA responsible for tracking and architectural oversight | - |
| **Target Date** | Date | Yes | Planned production implementation date | - |
| **Current Stage Gate** | Choice | Yes | Active governance gate | See Stage Gate Values section below |
| **Notes** | Multiple Lines Text | No | Additional context, updates, or relevant information | Recommended |
| **Attachments** | Attachment | No | Supporting documents, diagrams, or artifacts | - |

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#stage-gate-values]

#### Stage Gate Values

| Stage Gate | Description | Gate Reference |
| ---------- | ----------- | -------------- |
| **Initial** | Initiative identified but not yet started | - |
| **Started** | Initiative has begun preliminary work | - |
| **Conceptual Review (CRB)** | Work begins on inputs for Concept Review Board evaluation | [Gate 1](./architecture-governance.md#31-conceptual-review-board-crb) |
| **Logical Architecture Review (ARB)** | Work begins on inputs for Architecture Review Board review | [Gate 2](./architecture-governance.md#33-architecture-review-board-arb) |
| **Design Build and Test (SDLC)** | In software development lifecycle phase | - |
| **Change Control Review (CCB)** | Under Change Control Board review | [Gate 2A](./architecture-governance.md#22-flexible-gated-governance-process) |
| **Deploy to Staging / UAT** | Deployment to staging or UAT environment | - |
| **Operation Readiness Test Review (ORT)** | Under Operational Readiness Test Review | [Gate 3](./architecture-governance.md#34-operational-readiness-test-ort) |
| **Data Load / Conversion** | Data migration and conversion activities | - |
| **User Acceptance Test (UAT)** | User acceptance testing phase | - |
| **Turnover to Operations (TOPS)** | Transitioning to operations support | [Gate 4](./architecture-governance.md#35-turnover-to-operations-tops) |
| **Go Live** | Production deployment and go-live | - |
| **Post Production Review (PPR)** | Post-production review and assessment | [Gate 5](./architecture-governance.md#36-post-project-review-ppr) |
| **Completed** | Initiative successfully completed | - |
| **Cancelled** | Initiative discontinued | - |

#### Health Status Values

| Status | Color | Description |
| ------ | ----- | ----------- |
| **Initial** | ⚪ Grey | Initiative identified and entered into tracker, not yet started |
| **Active** | 🔵 Light Blue | Initiative is in progress and on track |
| **Late** | 🟡 Yellow | Initiative is behind schedule or experiencing delays |
| **Completed** | 🟢 Green | Initiative successfully completed |
| **Cancelled** | 🔴 Red | Initiative discontinued before completion |
page_texts.14:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#resources--timeline]

#### Resources & Timeline

- **Start Date**: Actual start date of initiative execution
- **Target Date**: Planned production implementation date
- **Actual Completion Date**: When achieved
page_texts.15:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#progress--health]

#### Progress & Health

- **Current Stage Gate**: Active governance gate (see Stage Gate Values below)
- **Gate Start Date**: When current gate phase began *(applies to CRB through PPR gates)*
- **Gate End Date**: When current gate phase completed *(applies to CRB through PPR gates; Go Live uses single date only)*
- **Health Status**: Initiative health indicator (see Health Status Values below)
- **Notes**: Additional context, updates, or relevant information

**Note**: Stage gates from Conceptual Review (CRB) through Post Production Review (PPR) track both begin and end dates to accurately reflect the duration of each governance phase. Go Live is the exception, tracking only a single date representing the production deployment moment.

page_texts.16:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#updating-weekly-status]

## Updating Weekly Status

As part of the weekly review cycle, Solution Architects must update the **Current Stage Gate** field along with the associated gate dates. These dates are critical for tracking governance progress and measuring gate durations.
page_texts.17:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#gate-date-guidelines]

### Gate Date Guidelines

When an initiative moves to a new stage gate or remains in an active governance gate:

**Gate Start Date**: Set this to the date when work **begins on preparing inputs** for the governance review. This typically includes:

- Gathering required documentation
- Preparing presentation materials
- Compiling artifacts needed for the review
- Scheduling the governance board meeting

**Gate End Date**: Set this to the date when the governance review is **finalized with a decision**. This occurs when:

- The governing body approves the initiative to proceed
- A conditional approval is granted with specific requirements
- The initiative is sent back for additional work
- Any other final status is determined by the governance board
page_texts.18:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#important-notes]

### Important Notes

- **Do not set Gate End Date** until the governance review has reached a final decision
- Gate Start Date may be several days or weeks before the actual review meeting
- For initiatives in "Go Live" status, only the Go Live date is tracked (no separate start/end dates)
- Updates to gate dates should occur during the weekly status update cycle
- Gate duration metrics are calculated automatically based on these dates
page_texts.19:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#initiative-lifecycle-progression]

### Initiative Lifecycle Progression

Initiatives should progress through stage gates in the order presented in the [Stage Gate Values](#stage-gate-values) table. Not all initiatives will require every stage gate—Solution Architects should select only the gates relevant to their specific initiative.

**Key Principles for Lifecycle Management:**

1. **Sequential Progression**: Stage gates should advance in the order listed in the Stage Gate Values table
2. **Chronological Dates**: All gate start and end dates must be in ascending chronological order as the initiative progresses
3. **Skip Irrelevant Gates**: Initiatives may skip stage gates that don't apply to their specific context
4. **Maintain Date Integrity**: When updating the current stage gate, ensure all previous gate dates are accurate and chronological
5. **Validate Historical Accuracy**: During weekly updates, verify that past gate dates correctly reflect when work actually occurred

**Example Progression:**

An initiative might flow as: *Initial* → *Started* → *Conceptual Review (CRB)* → *Logical Architecture Review (ARB)* → *Design Build and Test (SDLC)* → *Operation Readiness Test Review (ORT)* → *Turnover to Operations (TOPS)* → *Go Live* → *Post Production Review (PPR)* → Completed*

Another initiative might skip gates: *Initial* → *Started* → *Design Build and Test (SDLC)* → *Deploy to Staging / UAT* → *User Acceptance Test (UAT)* → *Go Live* → *Completed*

**Solution Architect Responsibilities:**

- Select appropriate stage gates based on initiative characteristics
- Ensure gate progression follows the sequential order in the Stage Gate Values table
- Verify all dates are chronological (earlier gates have earlier dates than later gates)
- Correct any out-of-sequence dates during weekly status reviews
- Document reasons for skipping stage gates in the Notes field

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#business-area-lead---strategic-direction]

### Business Area Lead - Strategic Direction

**Primary responsibility**: Provides business context, priorities, and strategic direction for initiatives within their area.

- **Identifies** strategic initiatives requiring architectural support
- **Communicates** business objectives and expected outcomes
- **Provides** business context and priority for initiatives
- **Secures** funding and resource commitments
- **Reviews** initiative progress and business alignment
- **Makes** business decisions and trade-offs
- **Champions** initiatives within the business organization
- **Participates** in reviews as needed
- **Approves** major scope or direction changes
- **Validates** business value and outcomes
page_texts.22:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#solution-architect-sa---initiative-lead]

### Solution Architect (SA) - Initiative Lead

**Primary responsibility**: Leads and tracks architecturally significant initiatives within their assigned business capability area.

- **Determines** architectural significance of initiatives in their domain
- **Decides** which initiatives require EA tracking and oversight
- **Creates** initiative entries in the tracker
- **Defines** scope, objectives, success criteria, and metrics
- **Maintains** tracker with current status and progress information
- **Provides** weekly status updates to EA Practice and Business Area Lead
- **Coordinates** initiative execution and delivery activities
- **Identifies** and manages risks, issues, and dependencies
- **Ensures** alignment with business capability strategy
- **Reviews** and validates technical approaches and decisions
- **Reports** capability area portfolio status
- **Participates** in monthly reviews with EA Governance Lead
- **Updates** completion status and outcomes
page_texts.23:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#ea-governance-lead---oversight--governance]

### EA Governance Lead - Oversight & Governance

**Primary responsibility**: Provides architectural oversight, governance, and cross-capability coordination.

- **Reviews** initiatives for architectural alignment and enterprise consistency
- **Approves** new initiatives for tracking
- **Conducts** monthly progress reviews with Solution Architects
- **Facilitates** dependency management across capability areas
- **Provides** strategic architectural guidance and support
- **Maintains** overall tracker health and integrity
- **Coordinates** with Solution Architects across all capability areas
- **Escalates** strategic concerns when needed
- **Conducts** post-implementation reviews
- **Reports** portfolio-level status and metrics
- **Ensures** best practices and standards compliance

---

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#weekly-updates-solution-architect]

### Weekly Updates (Solution Architect)

- Progress on deliverables
- Accomplishments this week
- Plans for next week
- New or changed risks
- Required decisions or support
- Updates to tracker status
- **Current stage gate status and progression**
- **Gate start and end dates** (update as initiative moves through governance gates)
page_texts.26:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#monthly-reviews-ea-governance-lead-with-solution-architects]

### Monthly Reviews (EA Governance Lead with Solution Architects)

- Overall portfolio health across all capability areas
- Initiative progress and health status
- Cross-initiative dependencies
- Strategic alignment check
- Resource utilization patterns
- Emerging trends or issues
- Architectural guidance and support needs

---
page_texts.28:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#dashboard-metrics]

### Dashboard Metrics

**Portfolio Health**

- Total active initiatives
- Initiatives by business capability area
- Initiatives by health status
- Initiatives by current stage gate

**Progress Metrics**

- Initiatives by effort size (Small, Medium, Large)
- On-time delivery (comparing Actual Completion Date to Target Date)
- Average time to complete by effort size
- Initiatives by assigned Solution Architect

**Timeline Metrics**

- Initiatives with Start Date set
- Initiatives past Target Date without Actual Completion Date
- Average gate duration (Gate Start Date to Gate End Date)
page_texts.29:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#standard-reports]

### Standard Reports

1. **Executive Dashboard**: High-level portfolio overview by business area
2. **Initiative Status Report**: Current stage gate, health status, and notes per initiative
3. **SA Portfolio View**: Initiatives grouped by assigned Solution Architect
4. **Timeline Report**: Start dates, target dates, and actual completion dates
5. **Gate Progress Report**: Current gate status and duration for all active initiatives

---
page_texts.31:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#for-solution-architects-initiative-leads]

### For Solution Architects (Initiative Leads)

✅ **Do:**

- Update status weekly, even if no change
- Be transparent about risks and issues early
- Maintain accurate completion percentages
- Document decisions and rationale
- Communicate proactively with EA Governance Lead and Business Area Lead
- Request help when blocked
- Apply architectural significance criteria consistently
- Coordinate with other SAs on dependencies

❌ **Don't:**

- Let status go stale for weeks
- Surprise Business Area Lead with bad news
- Inflate progress to look good
- Ignore cross-capability dependencies
- Work in isolation from EA Practice
- Track every initiative (only architecturally significant ones)
- Assume others know your status
page_texts.32:
[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#for-the-tracking-system]

### For the Tracking System

✅ **Do:**

- Use consistent naming conventions
- Tag initiatives with relevant metadata
- Attach supporting documentation
- Archive completed initiatives
- Clean up cancelled or stale items

❌ **Don't:**

- Create duplicate entries
- Use vague or unclear titles
- Skip required fields
- Lose historical data
- Let tracker become cluttered

[governance/processes/strategic-initiative-tracking.md#success-criteria]

## Success Criteria

This process is effective when:

- ✅ All strategic EA initiatives are tracked in the system
- ✅ Status is current within the past 7 days
- ✅ Stakeholders have visibility into progress
- ✅ Dependencies are identified and managed
- ✅ Risks are identified early and mitigated
- ✅ Resource conflicts are resolved proactively
- ✅ Initiatives align with strategic objectives
- ✅ Completion rates meet or exceed targets
- ✅ Lessons learned are captured and applied
